Ready for review. No blocking issues. ## Overview Online FP8 prefill for Kimi-K3 on MI355X is slower than BF16 today. This PR quantizes `routed_expert_down_proj` online and builds AITER's tuned GEMMs at startup. ## Claims - `routed_expert_down_proj` follows the online quantization config. Its checkpoint weights are BF16, so the checkpoint config is still bypassed. - `kernel_config.enable_rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup` (off by default) runs one dummy forward per AITER GEMM M bucket during kernel warmup. - Kimi-K3 agentic PD benchmark, with in_proj padded to 128 on AITER v0.1.24.post1: +2.1% total tok/s/GPU and mean TTFT 5.35 s to 4.05 s over online FP8 prefill without this PR, +0.7% over BF16 prefill. ## Validation - New `test_rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup.py` covers bucket coverage and the opt-in. A new KDA online-loading test checks the alignment padding: loading completes after six shards and the padding stays zero. pre-commit clean; GPU reload tests in `test_reload.py` not run. - End to end: one run per configuration, below. No accuracy evaluation. Variance not measured; the closest pair, BF16 with and without warmup, differs by 0.4% in throughput and 0.01 s / 1.2 s in mean / p90 TTFT. - KDA in_proj keeps main's 16-row alignment: AITER v0.1.27, main's pin, tunes 6288x7168 at the latency of 6400x7168. Not re-run end to end on v0.1.27.
End-to-end benchmark Kimi-K3, agentic multi-turn trace at concurrency 48, 1 prefill + 1 decode instance on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X, TP8 + DCP8, FP8 KV cache, MoRIIO. vLLM ROCm nightly `81198e97` with these changes mounted as file overlays. Online FP8 prefill means `--quantization-config` with `fp8_per_channel` targets on the attention projections, shared experts and dense MLPs, plus `re:.*\.routed_expert_down_proj$: mxfp4` and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1` from the down_proj step on. | Prefill | Run | Total tok/s/GPU | TTFT mean / p90 | |---|---|---|---| | BF16 GEMMs | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39140308384) | 10775 | 4.50 s / 9.22 s | | Online FP8 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39226586488) | 10626 | 5.35 s / 13.31 s | | + down_proj MXFP4 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39253422535) | 10663 | 5.14 s / 12.73 s | | + in_proj pad 128 | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39260261980) | 10552 | 5.78 s / 14.18 s | | + GEMM warmup (this PR) | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39352208397) | 10851 | 4.05 s / 8.50 s | | BF16 GEMMs + warmup only | [run](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39487012805) | 10729 | 4.51 s / 10.45 s | The `+ in_proj pad 128` step was needed on that nightly's AITER v0.1.24.post1, whose table tunes 6400x7168 but not 6288x7168; this PR no longer pads. In v0.1.27's `a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv` (gfx950, 256 CUs) the 6288/6400 latency ratio has median 1.00 and range 0.92 to 1.09 over the 52 M values from 256 to 8192, and both shapes use the same FlyDSL kernel at M=8192. Padding alone is slower because the newly tuned kernels are built on first use while serving; the warmup moves that to startup. Warmup without online quantization gives no gain. Load-time checks: 92 `routed_expert_down_proj` on `Mxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`, 69 `in_proj_qkvgfab` on `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel`.
## Details - Warmup sizes: AITER buckets up to `max_num_batched_tokens`, multiples of 8 up to 512, and `max_num_batched_tokens - 1` for Triton's divisibility specialization; 164 forwards at 8192 tokens, 541 to 585 s on the Kimi-K3 prefill instance (104 s without online quantization). The measured runs added a second timing sweep, dropped here. - An online config whose `linear` default does not ignore `routed_expert_down_proj` now quantizes it; add it to `ignore` to keep BF16. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @whx-sjtu.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Correct approach for FP8 prefill GEMMs: pad KDA in_proj to the tuned AITER shape and keep specialized decode reading the first 6288 rows. Keeping gemm warmup opt-in and off by default is right. One ask: the e2e table is a single run per config — please note run-to-run variance or add a second seed before treating the TTFT drop as firm.

Round 2 pushed 20af193: KDA in_proj keeps main's 16-row alignment (see the kda.py thread). @ChuanLi1101 variance is now noted under Validation: one run per configuration, and the closest pair (BF16 with and without warmup) differs by 0.4% in throughput and 0.01 s in mean TTFT, well below the 1.3 s TTFT drop.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

The premise here ("6288 has no entry and falls back to `torch._scaled_mm`") seems to hold only for the AITER version used in the benchmark nightly (`81198e97` pins `v0.1.24.post1`). main now pins AITER `v0.1.27` (#63774), and its `model_configs/a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv` has gfx950/256-CU entries for both N=6288,K=7168 and N=6400,K=7168 (62 M values each), with near-identical tuned latencies (e.g. M=8192: 299.7 us vs 294.7 us). On current main, 6288 should already dispatch to `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, so the unconditional 128 padding would only add ~1.8% rows on every arch/dtype. Could you re-measure 16-alignment vs 128-alignment (both with warmup) on `v0.1.27`, and drop the padding + guard change if there is no difference?

+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.model_executor.warmup.kernel_warmup import (
+    _aiter_gemm_m_buckets,
+    _rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+
+def _aiter_padded_m(m: int) -> int:
+    # AITER getPaddedM(M, N, K, gl=0) for M >= 16.
+    if m <= 256:
+        return (m + 15) // 16 * 16
+    if m <= 1024:
+        return (m + 31) // 32 * 32
+    if m <= 4096:
+        return (m + 63) // 64 * 64
+    return (m + 127) // 128 * 128
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("max_m", [1, 10, 16, 255, 1000, 4096, 5000, 8192])
+def test_buckets_reach_every_padded_m(max_m: int) -> None:
+    buckets = _aiter_gemm_m_buckets(max_m)
+    assert buckets == sorted(set(buckets))
+    assert buckets[-1] == max_m
+    assert all(_aiter_padded_m(b) == b for b in buckets[:-1] if b >= 16)
+    reachable = {_aiter_padded_m(m) for m in range(16, max_m + 1)}
+    assert reachable <= {_aiter_padded_m(b) for b in buckets if b >= 16}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enabled", [False, True])
+def test_warmup_runs_each_size_once_when_enabled(enabled: bool) -> None:
+    calls = []
+    worker = SimpleNamespace(
+        vllm_config=SimpleNamespace(
+            kernel_config=SimpleNamespace(enable_rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup=enabled)
+        ),
+        scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(max_num_batched_tokens=512),
+        model_runner=SimpleNamespace(
+            _dummy_run=lambda num_tokens, **kwargs: calls.append((num_tokens, kwargs))
+        ),
+    )
+    _rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup(worker)
+    if not enabled:
+        assert calls == []
+        return
+    sizes = [num_tokens for num_tokens, _ in calls]
+    assert sizes == sorted(set(sizes))
+    assert {1, 2, 4, 8, 504, 511, 512} <= set(sizes)
+    assert all(kwargs == {"skip_eplb": True} for _, kwargs in calls)

+def _aiter_gemm_m_buckets(max_m: int) -> list[int]:
+    """One token count per AITER tuned-GEMM bucket up to ``max_m``.
+
+    AITER pads M to 1, 2, 4 or 8 below 16, then to multiples of 16 / 32 / 64 /
+    128 up to 256 / 1024 / 4096 / beyond, and builds each bucket's kernel on
+    first use.
+    """
+    buckets = [m for m in (1, 2, 4, 8) if m <= max_m]
+    for step, upper in ((16, 256), (32, 1024), (64, 4096), (128, max_m)):
+        start = (buckets[-1] // step + 1) * step if buckets else step
+        buckets.extend(range(start, min(upper, max_m) + 1, step))
+    if max_m > 0 and buckets[-1] != max_m:
+        buckets.append(max_m)
+    return buckets
+
+
+def _rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup(worker: "Worker") -> None:
+    if not worker.vllm_config.kernel_config.enable_rocm_aiter_gemm_warmup:
+        return
+    max_m = worker.scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens
+    # Other AITER tables key exact M at multiples of 8 up to 512; max_m - 1
+    # covers Triton's divisibility specialization.
+    sizes = sorted(
+        {
+            m
+            for m in (
+                *_aiter_gemm_m_buckets(max_m),
+                *range(8, min(512, max_m) + 1, 8),
+                max_m - 1,
+            )
+            if m > 0
+        }
+    )
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    for num_tokens in sizes:
+        worker.model_runner._dummy_run(num_tokens, skip_eplb=True)
+    logger.info(
+        "Warmed up AITER GEMMs at %d token counts in %.1fs.",
+        len(sizes),
+        time.perf_counter() - start,
+    )
+
+

inline_comments.body: The premise here ("6288 has no entry and falls back to `torch._scaled_mm`") seems to hold only for the AITER version used in the benchmark nightly (`81198e97` pins `v0.1.24.post1`). main now pins AITER `v0.1.27` (#63774), and its `model_configs/a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv` has gfx950/256-CU entries for both N=6288,K=7168 and N=6400,K=7168 (62 M values each), with near-identical tuned latencies (e.g. M=8192: 299.7 us vs 294.7 us). On current main, 6288 should already dispatch to `AiterPreshuffledPerTokenFp8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, so the unconditional 128 padding would only add ~1.8% rows on every arch/dtype. Could you re-measure 16-alignment vs 128-alignment (both with warmup) on `v0.1.27`, and drop the padding + guard change if there is no difference?
